name: Perch Lake Campground
note: Rusk County Parks campground in the Rusk County Forest, on a wooded rise beside the man-made Perch Lake about 12 mi NW of Bruce and half a mile from Audie Lake Campground: one one-way gravel loop with a log pavilion. Unlike the county's other campgrounds, ATVs and UTVs may be ridden in the campground, and an ATV trail leaves from the loop. Sites 7 and 8 look at the lake through the trees. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Rusk County Parks reservation site (Konect, read 2026-11-17): Perch Lake Campground page ('campsites equipped with water and electricity'; 'Each campsite has 3 outlets for electricity: a 20-amp, a 30-amp, and a 50-amp'), campsite list SITE #1-#15, per-site pages 'RV Pad 46' X 14'' to 'RV Pad 86' X 14'' with Book Now buttons, campground map (one-way gravel loop, back-in pads), 15 site photos (gravel pads) -> current reservable county drive-in RV campground every site of which fits a 23-ft rig; county forestry page 'CAMPING IN RUSK COUNTY PARKS ARE OPEN YEAR ROUND! Campsites - $30'. Google Maps 'Audie Flowage-Perch Lake Campground' 4.7/72 with the county phone, pinned on this loop. Rules PDF: 'No horses'; ATVs allowed in the campground, but a general lake campground (pavilion, fishing lake, hunter walking trail), not an OHV staging camp (Keyes Lake rule, AWH 2026-11-17). Public (local): no price gate. Duplicate check 2026-11-17: no WI 'Perch Lake' entry but 3347 (USFS, Bayfield County, 96 km N); only entry within 5 km is 3593 Audie Lake Campground, 0.38 km SW, a separate county campground with its own entrance off Perch Lake Road, own sites and own booking page.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-17: Rusk County campground map (parks/i/lm/perch_lake3.jpg) puts sites 6-10 on the east side of the loop toward Perch Lake with forest between the pads and the shore; Esri World Imagery (1200 m, 440 m and 240 m frames centred 45.5510,-91.4265 / 45.5521,-91.4250 / 45.55255,-91.42340, all rendered): the east-side pads end ~35-40 m from the lake's pale sedge/drawdown shore band through continuous tree canopy, open water ~50-55 m out, no open apron and no pad on open ground by the water -> not lakefront. Official per-site photos (parks/i/ii/l__p7.jpg, l__p8.jpg, leaf-off) show Perch Lake through the trees behind the tables at sites 7 and 8 -> lakeview (filtered-view rule, AWH 2026-11-01); the other 13 photos show woods only. Campground DEM 470 m sits above the lake (DEM ~440-450 m), so no below-dam issue. Perch Lake is well over 5 acres (~270 x 480 m on imagery), so a lake, not a pond. --Claude

sites.note: 15 back-in sites with 50/30/20-amp electric and water. Posted pads run 46-86 ft by 14 ft (site 3 has no published page), so every listed site takes a 23-ft rig.

facilities.note: Water at the sites is off from about the second week of October to late April. Nearest dump: the Cenex in Weyerhaeuser or Rice Lake.

facilities_source: https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/camping/perch_lake_campground/ ('RV Dump stations are not available at the campground. Please utilize the Cenex gas station in Weyerhauser or Rice Lake.'; 'water gets turned off around the second week of October') + https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/alerts/635545b66fbe/ ('Water will be turned back on late April'), read 2026-11-17

season.note: Open year-round; water off in winter and sites are not plowed.

season_source: https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/ ('Rusk County Campgrounds are open year-round.') + https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/camping/perch_lake_campground/ ('Electricity remains on year-round') + https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/alerts/7b38031d1ed0/ ('Individual campsites are not snow plowed during winter months'), read 2026-11-17

fees.note: Rusk County Parks: $30 a night at every county campground. Each RV or camping unit on a site pays the fee; the 6-person cap does not apply when all campers are family.

fees_source: https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/ ('CAMPING FEES $30.00 per night.') + https://ruskcounty.org/forestry ('Campsites - $30') + https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/i/lr/perch_campground_rules_and_regulations.pdf ('Each RV or camping unit occupying a campsite must pay the required fee.'; 'A maximum of 6 persons per site. The only exception to this rule is if all campers are family members.'), read 2026-11-17

booking.note: Rusk County's own reservation site (Konect Parks), or the forestry office by phone. Reservations close 7 days before arrival; any site not reserved is first-come for that date. Only the current calendar year can be booked; next year's dates open January 1. Paid in full when booked, no refunds.

booking_source: https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/camping/perch_lake_campground/ ('All campsites reservations must be made seven or more days in advance otherwise they are first come'; 'There are no reimbursements for cancellations.') + https://parks.ruskcounty.org/parks/ ('Reservations are only available for the current calendar year. Reservations for the following year will open on January 1st of that year.') + https://ruskcounty.org/forestry ('Purchase online or call the office (715) 532-2113'), read 2026-11-17

flags: ATVs/UTVs are allowed IN this campground (county rules PDF: allowed at Perch Lake, prohibited at Audie, Josie Creek and Murphy) and the county map shows an ATV trail leaving the loop. Kept as a general lake campground under the Keyes Lake rule (AWH 2026-11-17); the note says so.
Site 3 is in the campsite list and on the map (with a photo, l__p3.jpg) but has no per-site page, so its pad length is unpublished; count 15 from the list.
Google's place is one combined listing, 'Audie Flowage-Perch Lake Campground' (4.7/72, pin 45.55181,-91.42427 on this loop). It may cover Audie Lake too; not checked.
Pin: centre of the loop from imagery (45.55240,-91.42470); the county address is W14634 Perch Lake Road, Weyerhaeuser.
